hot_threads.summary: Developers are discussing how to transition Bitcoin to quantum-resistant security without driving up transaction fees. They are also exploring decentralized storage-sharing techniques to keep running a Bitcoin node cheap and accessible for everyone.
hot_threads.technical_summary: The debate centers on the economic trade-offs of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) output types, specifically how larger signature sizes impact fee-rate sensitivity and user adoption. To mitigate the resulting blockchain bloat and its pressure on Initial Block Download (IBD) for non-pruned nodes, developers are proposing historical block storage sharding. By leveraging Forward Error Correction (FEC) techniques, nodes could store only a fraction of the blockchain history while maintaining data availability. Next steps require analyzing PQC layout efficiency and evaluating the peer-to-peer feasibility of FEC-sharding protocols.

The ongoing discussion, referencing historical threads, focuses on evaluating whether this narrower cryptographic primitive provides sufficient security while significantly improving performance.

Proving Bitcoin

Full block validity proofs generated from unmodified Bitcoin…
hot_threads.insight: The technical pivot focuses on whether the purity of running unmodified consensus code in a zkVM can ever be optimized enough to compete with the low cost of fraud-proof architectures.
hot_threads.summary: Developers are exploring running Bitcoin's official rules inside zero-knowledge proof software, which could let users instantly verify the blockchain's validity on simple devices. However, the high computational cost of creating these proofs remains a major hurdle compared to lighter verification methods.
hot_threads.technical_summary: This initiative compiles unmodified Bitcoin Core v28 consensus code to the RISC-V architecture to run within a zkVM, generating zero-knowledge block validity proofs. While this ensures perfect consensus compatibility, developers note that the generation costs are currently far more expensive than fraud-proof alternatives like Utreexo-based Floresta. Future work must focus on optimizing the prover efficiency, investigating recursive proof aggregation, and exploring untapped zkVM execution improvements.
